page.title: Creative Operations Setup Guide for Marketing Teams
page.description: Learn the roles, tools, metrics and rollout steps to build a creative ops function that cuts cycle time and keeps assets on brand.
page.h1: How to set up creative operations for a marketing team
page.definition: Creative operations is the system that connects intake, briefing, production, review, approval, publishing and reporting so marketing and content teams deliver assets on time and on brand. It assigns owners, sets cycle-time targets and chooses tools for work management, asset storage and review.
page.quick_answer: Start by naming one owner for each of the seven stages from intake to reporting, then pick a work-management tool and an asset library that integrate with your publishing stack.

sections.h2: What roles make up a creative ops team?

blocks.p: A full team covers five distinct roles, though small groups often combine them in one producer.

head: Role
Primary responsibility
rows: Owns workflow design, capacity planning and vendor contracts
Runs day-to-day intake, scheduling and status reporting
Briefs designers, manages review rounds and delivers final files
Tags, versions and governs the digital asset management library
Tracks cycle time, revision count, on-time rate and capacity use

sections.h2: Which tools support each stage of the creative workflow?

blocks.p: Match tool categories to the seven stages so hand-offs stay visible and searchable.

ul: Intake and calendar: Asana, Monday.com or Airtable
Briefs and specs: Google Docs or Notion
Work management: Adobe Workfront, Asana, Monday.com or Wrike
Design review: Figma for UI, Frame.io for video

sections.h2: How do you measure creative ops performance?

blocks.p: Track four core metrics that reveal bottlenecks and capacity gaps.

ul: Cycle time from approved brief to publish
On-time delivery rate against committed dates
Capacity utilisation across designers, writers and producers

sections.h2: When should you build creative ops in-house versus hire an agency?

blocks.p: Keep strategy, brand voice approval and product decisions inside; outsource moderation, member support, programming, onboarding and reporting when volume exceeds internal bandwidth.

ul: In-house: brand governance, campaign prioritisation, product launch sequencing
Outsource: high-volume asset production, localisation, routine QA and reporting
Hybrid: internal ops lead manages external production partners on fixed scopes

sections.h2: What does a 90-day creative ops rollout look like?

blocks.p: A first plan runs ninety days: long enough to see a trend, short enough to change course.

ol: Week one to two: audit current intake, tools and pain points; interview stakeholders
Week three: define seven-stage workflow, assign owners, select work-management tool
Week four: configure asset library taxonomy and permissions
Week five to six: pilot with two campaign types, measure cycle time and revisions
Week seven: refine templates, approval gates and reporting dashboards
Week eight to twelve: scale to all channels, train team, set quarterly review cadence

faq.q: How many revision rounds are typical for a long-form asset?
faq.a: Most teams see two to three rounds when briefs are complete; each extra round adds a day to cycle time and signals a briefing gap.

faq.q: What is the fastest way to reduce cycle time without hiring?
faq.a: Enforce a complete brief checklist at intake, lock approval gates to named stakeholders and automate hand-offs between work management and asset library.

faq.q: Which metric signals that creative ops is scaling well?
faq.a: On-time delivery rate above eighty percent while revision rounds stay flat or drop indicates the workflow absorbs volume without quality loss.

faq.q: Can a single producer run creative ops for a small team?
faq.a: Yes, one producer can combine operations lead, project manager and creative producer roles when asset volume stays below twenty pieces per month.
